description:
I'm an aspiring developer interested in space exploration, astronomy, and building interactive technology that makes complex scientific information easier to explore and understand.

I'm currently developing an exoplanet research and visualization project featuring interactive 3D planetary systems, exoplanet information, habitability zones, and scientific data visualizations. I enjoy experimenting with AI-assisted development, frontend engineering, and turning ideas into working prototypes.
summary:
Deep Field Observatory is an interactive astronomy research interface designed to make planetary and exoplanet information easier to explore. The project combines a 3D solar-system visualization, an exoplanet catalog, individual object detail panels, habitability-zone information, and scientific data visualizations in a unified observatory-style experience.

Users can explore selected celestial objects, inspect available properties such as distance, mass, radius, and discovery year, and view information through a focused scientific interface. The project aims to make complex astronomical concepts more accessible through interactive visualization and clear presentation of scientific information.

The current version is an exploratory prototype related to the broader astrophysics theme of Planet X and SPHEREx. It does not yet implement the challenge's core SPHEREx sky-image time-series comparison functionality or integrate SPHEREx observations. Some catalog values and visualizations are demonstration data, and unavailable or unverified information is identified accordingly.
details:
Deep Field Observatory is an interactive web-based astronomy research prototype built to bring planetary and exoplanet information into one accessible scientific interface.

The application features a 3D visualization of selected solar-system objects, an exoplanet discovery catalog, individual object detail panels, habitability-zone visualization, and an analytics dashboard. Users can select celestial objects, explore their available properties, and navigate between different research views.

The project is designed around the idea of a digital observatory: instead of presenting astronomical information as disconnected tables, it combines visual exploration with structured scientific readouts. Its intended benefit is to make astronomy more approachable while helping users understand the relationships between planetary properties and habitability concepts.

The interface was developed using Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Three.js, React Three Fiber, and Recharts. AI-assisted development tools were used to support coding, debugging, and documentation.

The project is an exploratory prototype related to the astrophysics theme of Planet X and SPHEREx. It does not currently display actual SPHEREx observations, compare SPHEREx images over time, or provide the challenge's requested coordinate-based image viewer. These are important future development areas.

Some catalog entries and visualizations use demonstration data rather than live mission feeds. Missing or unverified information is identified in the interface rather than presented as confirmed scientific data.
